source_review.notes: Checked all ten references. Reviewed the Lamport, Adve-Gharachorloo, x86-TSO, Boehm-Adve, and Batty primary sources for their stated scope. Checked the current C++ draft as-if and data-race clauses; Java SE 26 Chapter 17 program-order, execution, volatile, synchronizes-with, happens-before, and causality rules; Intel SDM version 092 memory-ordering location; current Arm A-profile memory-model guidance; and the current Go memory model against primary or official sources.

evidence: Reviewed program order po, reads-from rf, per-location modification order mo_x, synchronizes-with sw, happens-before hb, SC total order, stores S_i, loads L_i, and buffer drains F_i.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The chapter distinguishes total orders, partial-order edges, abstract executions, implementation mappings, and physical mechanisms.

evidence: Independently enumerated all 4! permutations and confirmed 6 respect S0<L0 and S1<L1, yielding 01 once, 10 once, 11 four times, and 00 zero times.
Independently enumerated all 6! permutations with S0 before L0/F0 and S1 before L1/F1; confirmed 80 valid buffered schedules yielding 00:18, 01:22, 10:22, and 11:18.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts match exact executable stdout and are explicitly not treated as probabilities.

evidence: Re-derived the SC all-zero contradiction S0<L0<S1<L1<S0.
Re-derived the buffered witness S0,S1,L0,L1,F0,F1 for all-zero.
Re-derived the message-publication chain payload-write sequenced-before release, release synchronizes-with observing acquire, acquire sequenced-before payload-read.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The proof never treats store-buffer schedules as source-language permission without a mapping argument.

evidence: Reviewed racy plain flags, dead-store elimination, load reuse, hidden raw fences, store buffering, per-location coherence, relaxed publication, unrelated acquire reads, volatile differences, target changes, negative stress evidence, speculative side channels, device/DMA memory, and safety-critical transfer.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Language, compiler, ISA, microarchitecture, device, and empirical boundaries are kept explicit.

evidence: Checked preservation of intra-thread semantics, source-defined observation, per-thread store-before-load constraints, SC program-order preservation, single-location coherence scope, source synchronization requirements, and version/target assumptions.
invariant_checking.notes: Atomicity is not promoted to ordering, coherence is not promoted to consistency, and compiler barriers are not promoted to hardware fences.

Checked the SC impossibility proof, buffered possibility witness, publication proof, data-race counterexamples, and evidence hierarchy.
proof_review.notes: Allowed behavior, likely mechanism, empirical observation, security mitigation, timing, and safety assurance remain distinct claims.

evidence: Audited the schematic transformation fragment, SC cycle proof, store-buffer model, message-passing argument, compiler/processor descriptions, device caveat, and safety-critical example.

evidence: Reproduced the deterministic enumeration with Python 3.14.4: 6 SC schedules and 80 buffered schedules with exact outcome counts.
Confirmed one intentionally schematic source fragment is skipped and no executable route is unavailable.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The chapter explicitly rejects interpreting schedule counts as probabilities or unobserved outcomes as forbidden.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed distinctions among program order, compiler transformation, emitted order, issue/completion/retirement, visibility, store buffering, coherence, consistency, memory models, data races, barriers, fences, atomics, volatile, and device memory.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed source-first proof, versioned compiler/target mappings, optimized assembly, IR, litmus models, race detectors, stress limitations, logging perturbation, cross-architecture portability, speculative security, DMA, I/O barriers, cache maintenance, and target-specific review.

pedagogical_review.notes: The chapter moves from the contract stack through compiler and processor mechanisms to SC and buffered litmus reasoning, publication, barrier taxonomy, device boundaries, evidence, ten distinct examples, and five exercises progressing to DMA safety transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, practitioner, compiler, processor, driver, medical, clinical, railway, hardware, real-time, speculative-execution, functional-safety, cybersecurity, certification, regulatory, quality, or human-factors review is claimed. Finite schedule enumeration, source checking, and manual reasoning do not prove a real program data-race-free, a compiler mapping sound, a processor conformant, a device protocol ordered, a security mitigation sufficient, a deadline met, or deployment safe.
